Course Project · ENES100

Over-Terrain Vehicle

Designed the magnetic-puck detection subsystem — from Faraday induction modeling to Hall-effect sensor implementation.

Course: ENES100 — Introduction to Engineering Design

Team project

My role: Magnetic detection subsystem design and electronics

Problem

Build an autonomous vehicle capable of navigating over rough terrain and detecting a hidden magnetic puck. The detection subsystem needed to reliably identify the puck's location as the vehicle traversed the course.

Approach

I initially modeled a Faraday induction coil approach, analyzing the induced EMF as the vehicle passed over the magnetic puck. After evaluating signal-to-noise characteristics, I pivoted to a Hall-effect sensorfor more reliable detection at the speeds and distances involved.

I co-wired the Arduino electronics, integrating the Hall-effect sensor with the vehicle's main control board and writing the detection threshold logic.
